config.title: Push Notification Handler

intro.title: Push Notification Handler
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a push notification handler for your Ionic Angular app. You will learn how to listen for incoming push notifications when your app is open. The core concept involves subscribing to notification events using Capacitor's Push Notifications API. You will work with TypeScript services and event listeners to display notification data. By the end, you'll have a functional handler that logs and shows notifications within your app.
intro.usecase: Push notifications are essential in modern mobile apps for user engagement and timely information delivery. In e-commerce apps like Amazon or eBay, they alert users about order confirmations, shipping updates, and flash sales. Social media platforms like Instagram use them to notify about new messages, likes, or comments. Fitness apps like Strava send notifications for workout reminders and achievement milestones. As a developer, implementing proper notification handlers ensures your app can receive, process, and display these critical messages even when the app is in the background.

objectives: Import the necessary Capacitor Push Notifications plugin into an Angular service
Define a service class with proper dependency injection for notification handling
Implement a method to request push notification permissions from the user
Utilize the register method to obtain a device token for push notifications
Handle incoming push notification payloads by extracting data from notification objects
Apply event listeners to respond to notification taps and foreground/background states
Construct notification display logic to show alerts when the app is in the foreground
Store device tokens in a component state variable for later use
Invoke notification permission requests from a component lifecycle hook
Control notification behavior based on app state (foreground/background)
Return appropriate responses from notification handler methods
Modify component templates to include buttons that trigger notification setup

steps.title: Import Capacitor Push Notifications plugin
steps.instruction: Import the PushNotifications plugin from the @capacitor/push-notifications package.
steps.hint: Use the standard ES6 import syntax to import PushNotifications from '@capacitor/push-notifications'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing a Capacitor plugin
import { PushNotifications } from '@capacitor/push-notifications';
steps.expectedOutcome: The PushNotifications plugin is imported and available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement for PushNotifications from '@capacitor/push-notifications' is correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the PushNotifications plugin. This gives you access to Capacitor's push notification APIs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing PushNotifications from the correct package '@capacitor/push-notifications'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import PushNotifications from '@capacitor/push-notifications'.

steps.title: Import Ionic UI components
steps.instruction: Add import statements for IonButton, IonCard, IonCardContent, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, and IonContent from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the component names in curly braces, then from and the package path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing Ionic components
import { IonButton, IonCard, IonCardContent } from '@ionic/angular/standalone';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Ionic components IonButton, IonCard, IonCardContent, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, and IonContent are imported and ready to be used in the component.
successCriteria: The import statement includes all six components from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Ionic UI components needed for building the notification interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some components, but make sure to include all six: IonButton, IonCard, IonCardContent, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, and IonContent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing from '@ionic/angular/standalone' and including all six components.

steps.title: Import Angular core dependencies
steps.instruction: Add import statements for Component and OnInit from @angular/core.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing Angular core dependencies
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have import statements for Component and OnInit from @angular/core, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: The import statement for Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' is correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Angular core dependencies Component and OnInit. These are essential for creating Angular components and implementing lifecycle hooks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's something missing. Make sure you're importing both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' using the correct import syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' to use Angular's component decorator and lifecycle hooks.

steps.title: Create the component class
steps.instruction: Create a class named PushNotificationHandlerComponent that implements the OnInit interface from Angular core.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define this as an Angular component. The class should have an empty ngOnInit method for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named PushNotificationHandlerComponent is created with the @Component decorator and implements OnInit.
successCriteria: The code should include: 1) @Component decorator with selector and template properties, 2) class named PushNotificationHandlerComponent, 3) implements OnInit interface, 4) empty ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the PushNotificationHandlerComponent class with the proper Angular structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component has all required elements: @Component decorator, correct class name, implements OnInit, and an ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you have the @Component decorator, correct class name, and that it implements OnInit with an ngOnInit method.

steps.title: Initialize notification status property
steps.instruction: Inside the component class, add a public property called 'notificationStatus' with type 'string' and initial value 'Checking...'.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body, like 'notificationStatus: string = 'Checking...';'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has a 'notificationStatus' property that can be used to track and display the current notification permission status.
successCriteria: The component class contains a public property named 'notificationStatus' with type 'string' and initial value 'Checking...'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the notificationStatus property to track permission status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check: Is it named exactly 'notificationStatus'? Does it have type 'string'? Is its initial value 'Checking...'?
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't yet have the required notificationStatus property. Add a public property called 'notificationStatus' with type 'string' and initial value 'Checking...' inside the class.

steps.title: Define requestPermission method
steps.instruction: Inside the PushNotificationHandlerComponent class, add an async method called requestPermission that calls PushNotifications.requestPermissions() and updates the notificationStatus property.
steps.hint: Remember to use the async keyword before the method name and await the PushNotifications.requestPermissions() call. Update notificationStatus with the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has an async requestPermission method that calls the Capacitor Push Notifications API and updates the notificationStatus property.
successCriteria: The method should be named requestPermission, be async, call PushNotifications.requestPermissions(), and update notificationStatus with the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the requestPermission method that will handle permission requests for push notifications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your method is async, properly calls PushNotifications.requestPermissions(), and updates notificationStatus with the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method doesn't match the requirements. Make sure you create an async method called requestPermission that calls PushNotifications.requestPermissions() and updates notificationStatus.

steps.title: Define checkPermission method
steps.instruction: Add an async method called checkPermission to your component class. Inside this method, call PushNotifications.checkPermissions() and update the notificationStatus property with the result.
steps.hint: Remember to use async/await syntax and update the notificationStatus property with the permission status you get from the API call.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async checkPermission method that calls the Capacitor Push Notifications API and updates the component's notificationStatus property.
successCriteria:
The component class contains an async method named checkPermission that:
1. Calls PushNotifications.checkPermissions()
2. Updates the notificationStatus property with the permission result
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully created the checkPermission method that queries the current notification permissions and updates the status. This method will be essential for checking the user's current permission state before requesting new permissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are a few issues. Make sure your method is async, properly calls PushNotifications.checkPermissions(), and updates the notificationStatus property with the result. Check that you're using await with the API call and assigning the permission status to this.notificationStatus.
steps.feedbackWrong: The checkPermission method is not correctly implemented. You need to create an async method that calls the Capacitor Push Notifications API to check permissions and updates the notificationStatus property. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Implement ngOnInit lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Inside the PushNotificationHandlerComponent class, implement the ngOnInit method to call the checkPermission method when the component initializes.
steps.hint: The ngOnInit method should be synchronous and call the existing checkPermission method.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically check notification permissions when it loads.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method should be implemented with a call to checkPermission().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented ngOnInit to automatically check permissions when the component loads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure ngOnInit calls checkPermission() exactly as shown.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method should call checkPermission() to initialize permission checking.

steps.title: Start the component template
steps.instruction: Add a basic template to your component that includes an IonContent wrapper component.
steps.hint: Replace the empty template string with an IonContent component that will wrap your future UI elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains an IonContent wrapper component.
successCriteria: The template property should contain '<ion-content></ion-content>' as the content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the IonContent wrapper to your component template. This provides the basic structure for your push notification UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the template needs to contain an IonContent component. Make sure you've added '<ion-content></ion-content>' inside the template string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template is still empty. You need to add an IonContent component to create the basic structure for your UI.

steps.title: Add notification status card
steps.instruction: Inside the component template, add an IonCard element that displays the current notification permission status. The card should contain an IonCardHeader with an IonCardTitle, and an IonCardContent that shows the notificationStatus property value.
steps.hint: Use Ionic's card components to create a structured display area for the status. The notificationStatus property is already defined in your component class.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of an Ionic card displaying a status value
<IonCard>
  <IonCardHeader>
    <IonCardTitle>Notification Status</IonCardTitle>
  </IonCardHeader>
  <IonCardContent>
    {{ status }}
  </IonCardContent>
</IonCard>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now includes an Ionic card that displays the current notification permission status using the notificationStatus property.
successCriteria: The template should contain an IonCard element with IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, and IonCardContent. The IonCardContent should display the notificationStatus property value using Angular interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added a notification status card that will display the current permission status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all the required card components: IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, and IonCardContent. Also ensure you're displaying the notificationStatus property value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the expected card structure. Remember to use Ionic's card components and display the notificationStatus property value.

steps.title: Add request permission button
steps.instruction: In the component template, add an IonButton with a click event bound to the requestPermission() method and set its label to 'Request Permission'.
steps.hint: Use the IonButton component with the (click) event binding and set the button text to 'Request Permission'.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding a button with click handler -->
<IonButton (click)="handleClick()">Click Me</IonButton>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain a button that triggers the requestPermission method when clicked.
successCriteria: The template includes an IonButton with (click)="requestPermission()" and the text 'Request Permission'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the request permission button with the correct click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it uses (click)="requestPermission()" and has the label 'Request Permission'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct click handler or label. Try adding an IonButton with (click)="requestPermission()" and text 'Request Permission'.

steps.title: Add check permission button
steps.instruction: In the component template, add an IonButton with a click event bound to the checkPermission() method and label it 'Check Permission'.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding to call the checkPermission method. The button should be placed after the existing request permission button.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding a button with click handler -->
<IonButton expand="block" (click)="checkPermission()">Check Permission</IonButton>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a second button that triggers the checkPermission method when clicked.
successCriteria: The code should include an IonButton element with (click)="checkPermission()" and the text 'Check Permission'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button to check the current notification permissions. The button is properly wired to call the checkPermission method when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might be missing the correct click handler or label. Make sure it has (click)="checkPermission()" and displays 'Check Permission'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button wasn't added correctly. You need to add an IonButton with (click)="checkPermission()" and the label 'Check Permission' in the template.
